job.style: a step-by-step explanation of a process

passage: Maps are essential tools for understanding our world, but they serve different purposes depending on their design. A political map focuses on administrative boundaries, showing states, capitals, and countries, whereas a physical map highlights natural features like mountains, plateaus, and rivers. When we need to represent a large area like a continent on a small sheet of paper, we use a small scale map. Conversely, a large scale map is used to show a small area, such as a village or a school, in great detail. Maps are not always oriented with North at the top; sometimes, a map may use a directional arrow to indicate North, which could be pointing in any direction. Finally, it is important to distinguish between a map and a sketch. A map is drawn to scale, ensuring accurate proportions, while a sketch is a drawing based on memory and spot observation without a scale. A sketch is not just a messy map; it is a specific type of informal drawing used for quick reference. By understanding these components, you can choose the right tool for your geographic needs.

items.evidence: A political map focuses on administrative boundaries, showing states, capitals, and countries, whereas a physical map highlights natural features like mountains, plateaus, and rivers.
items.q: Meena wants to study the mountains and rivers of India. Which map should she choose?
options: A physical map, which shows natural land features
A political map, which shows how high mountains are
A political map, which shows the same features
A political map, which shows states and capitals
items.explain: A physical map highlights natural features like mountains and rivers; a political map shows boundaries.

wrong.why: thinks political maps show mountain heights
thinks both maps are the same except colour
mixes up which map shows which features

items.evidence: When we need to represent a large area like a continent on a small sheet of paper, we use a small scale map.
items.q: Ravi must show all of Asia on one notebook page. Which map should he draw?
options: A small scale map of the whole continent
A large scale map, because the area is big
A small scale map showing every street clearly
A sketch, because it fits any large area
items.explain: A large area like a continent on a small sheet needs a small scale map.

wrong.why: thinks small scale maps show great detail
does not know a sketch is an informal drawing for quick reference

items.evidence: Maps are not always oriented with North at the top; sometimes, a map may use a directional arrow to indicate North, which could be pointing in any direction.
items.q: On Asha's map, the North arrow points to the left. How should she read the map?
options: Treat the left side of the map as North
Treat the top of the map as North anyway
Treat the map as wrongly drawn and useless
Treat the right side of the map as North
items.explain: North is not always at the top; the arrow shows North, whichever way it points.

wrong.why: thinks North is always at the top
thinks a map without North at the top is a mistake
reverses the direction of the arrow

items.evidence: A map is drawn to scale, ensuring accurate proportions, while a sketch is a drawing based on memory and spot observation without a scale.
items.q: Kabir draws his route to school from memory, without measuring anything. What has he made?
options: A sketch, which is drawn without any scale
A bad map, because it is not neat
A sketch, which must still be drawn to scale
A large scale map, as it shows a small area
items.explain: A sketch is drawn from memory and observation without scale; a map is drawn to scale.

wrong.why: thinks a sketch is just a messy map
links small area to large scale map, ignoring that no scale was used
